title: Our Approach
heading: Our Teaching and Learning Approach
seo_description: Explicit teaching, consistent routines and high expectations underpin teaching and learning at Ellenbrook Primary School. See how we help students succeed.

data.lead: At Ellenbrook Primary School, our focus is on ensuring every student experiences effective teaching that is clear, structured and designed to support strong learning progress.
data.body:
We use an explicit teaching approach that breaks learning into manageable steps, with teachers modelling new concepts, guiding students through practice, and supporting them to apply their skills independently with confidence.

Across the school, we maintain consistent routines and high expectations so that students can quickly engage in learning and understand what is expected of them in every classroom. This predictability supports student confidence and allows more time to be spent on learning itself.

We also place a strong emphasis on relationships, recognising that students learn best when they feel respected, supported and connected to their teacher and peers. Our classrooms are safe, calm and purposeful learning environments where all students are encouraged to achieve their personal best.

Our approach continues to evolve through collaboration, reflection and professional learning, ensuring our practice remains aligned with current research and best supports the needs of our students.

title: Teaching and Learning Handbook
heading: Overview of the Teaching and Learning Handbook
seo_description: Our Teaching and Learning Handbook sets out the shared, evidence-based approach that guides every classroom at Ellenbrook Primary School.

data.lead: At our school, we are committed to providing every student with high-quality teaching that is consistent, explicit, and grounded in evidence-based practice.
data.body:
Our Teaching & Learning Handbook outlines the shared approach that guides all classroom practice across the school. This handbook ensures that every student experiences a consistent learning environment, regardless of their classroom or year level. It supports teachers to deliver engaging, well-structured lessons that maximise student understanding, participation, and achievement.

Our shared approach to teaching

The Teaching & Learning Handbook provides the agreed framework that guides teaching and learning across Ellenbrook Primary School.

It sets out clear expectations for lesson design, curriculum delivery and classroom practice, ensuring a consistent approach across all year levels and learning areas. This supports smooth continuity in learning as students move through the school.

The handbook serves as a practical reference for staff, supporting planning, instruction and assessment, and ensuring alignment in how learning is delivered across the school.

Why consistency matters

Research shows that students learn more effectively when teaching practices are consistent and predictable. Our whole-school approach ensures:

  • Clear and consistent routines in every classroom
  • High expectations for all students
  • Reduced cognitive load so students can focus on learning
  • Strong foundations in literacy and numeracy
  • Equitable access to high-quality teaching for every child

What you will find in our handbook

  • Our school vision, values and expectations for a successful learning environment
  • Our whole-school instructional model, including lesson design and planning expectations
  • Evidence-based approaches to teaching English, including reading, phonics, spelling, fluency and comprehension
  • Structured approaches to mathematics, including number sense, mental maths, fluency and times tables
  • Details of key programs and resources used across the school to ensure consistent teaching practice
  • A shared framework that supports high-quality, consistent teaching and learning in every classroom

Our commitment to excellence

We are committed to continuous improvement and evidence-informed practice. The Teaching & Learning Handbook is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect current research and best practice in education.

Our goal is simple: to ensure every student is supported, challenged, and given the best opportunity to succeed for life-long learning.

View the handbook

Families are welcome to view the Teaching & Learning Handbook.

title: Assessment and Reporting
seo_description: Assessment and reporting at Ellenbrook Primary School, with formal reports twice a year and two Parent Interview Days, aligned to the WA Curriculum.

data.lead: At Ellenbrook Primary School, assessment is an integral part of the teaching and learning process. It helps teachers identify student strengths, monitor progress, and plan for future learning.
data.body:
Our assessment and reporting practices align with the Western Australian Department of Education's requirements and are designed to provide families with clear and meaningful information about their child's achievement and progress.

How we assess student learning

Teachers use a range of assessment methods throughout the year to gather evidence of student learning. These include classroom observations, work samples, teacher judgements, tests, and other assessment tasks.

In addition to year-level assessments, all teachers participate in a whole-school assessment schedule. This allows us to monitor student progress over time, identify trends, evaluate the effectiveness of teaching programs, and inform whole-school planning and improvement priorities.

Assessment information is used to:

  • Monitor individual student progress and achievement
  • Identify students requiring additional support or extension
  • Inform teaching and learning programs
  • Track progress across year levels and cohorts
  • Support whole-school improvement planning

Reporting to parents

Parents and carers receive formal reports twice each year in accordance with Department of Education requirements. These reports provide information about student achievement, effort, and progress against the Western Australian Curriculum.

To strengthen communication between home and school, Ellenbrook Primary School also provides two Parent Interview Days each year. These interviews offer families the opportunity to discuss their child's progress, celebrate successes, and work collaboratively with teachers to support future learning.
We value the important partnership between school and home and encourage families to engage with reporting and interview opportunities throughout the year.

title: IEC
heading: About the Intensive English Centre
seo_description: The Ellenbrook Intensive English Centre helps newly arrived Year 1 to 6 students learn English, with small classes, multilingual staff and free buses.

data.lead: The new Intensive English Centre at Ellenbrook Primary School opened in February 2025. It offers a specialised intensive English language program for newly arrived Year 1 to 6 students with limited or no English skills.
data.body: The program focuses on developing students' communication skills in English to help them integrate into mainstream schooling. The centre supports students in becoming fully integrated into the school community through participation in school-wide events such as assemblies and faction carnivals, as well as educational activities and social interactions.

Newly arrived? Under almost all circumstances, newly arrived students may be enrolled directly in the IEC rather than going through an enrolment process at another school first. To make an appointment, contact Mr Matt Bennett, IEC Deputy Principal, or Mrs Tracie Douglas, IEC School Officer, on 08 9297 7300.
About the program

items.title: Educational program details
items.body: The centre provides intensive English tuition for primary school students who come to Western Australia with limited English language capability. Participants may also be students who were born in Australia but have grown up speaking the home language until such time as they begin to participate in formalised schooling. Students typically spend one or two years in the Intensive English Centre, with funding allocated for each enrolled student and specialist staff enabling smaller class sizes.

items.title: Program benefits
items.body:
The Intensive English Centre offers:

  • Specialised intensive English language teaching support
  • One ethnic education assistant in each class who speaks multiple languages
  • Smaller class sizes (up to 15 or 16 students) supporting individualised learning
  • Cultural support in a nurturing environment
  • Free daily bus service for primary school-aged children

items.title: Curriculum and transition
items.body: The centre provides differentiated oral and written English learning programs based on the Western Australian Curriculum, targeting individual students' English language learning needs. Subjects studied with specialist teachers include Physical Education, Mathematics, Science, and the Arts. Teachers and IEC administration also work with students' schools of origin to support a smooth transition to mainstream classes.

items.title: Eligibility for the IEC
items.body:
Students are eligible if they:

  • are in the Beginning or Emerging Phase of learning Standard Australian English (SAE) in all language modes, as assessed using the English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) Progress Map
  • hold an eligible visa category or hold Australian citizenship
  • are in Years 1 to 6
  • are assessed as Stage 1*

*Stage 1:

  • Students born in Australia and enrolled in Year 1; or
  • Students who have been in Australia no longer than a year, enrolled within six months of arrival, and are in their first year of schooling in Australia; or
  • Students who have had limited schooling (less than three years of continuous schooling prior to arrival in Australia) and who are within the first two years of schooling in Australia.

items.title: Ellenbrook IEC classes
items.body:
The IEC began in early 2025 with eleven students in two Year 1/2 classes. We are now running three classes with 52 students from Years 1 to 6. Students from 23 distinct language groups are enrolled in our IEC.

We have what are known as Phase 1 and Phase 2 classes.

  • Phase 1 focuses on developing students' English oral language skills. Students also learn to read and write in English at this phase.
  • Phase 2 continues to develop and extend students' English oral language skills along with reading and writing skills.

The preferred ratio is 1 teacher to 16 students; however, fluctuations occur throughout the school year due to enrolments and transitions to mainstream schooling, which may result in numbers being lower or higher than 16 in a class.

items.title: Enrolments in the IEC program
items.body:
Ellenbrook Intensive English Centre (IEC) conducts continuous enrolments throughout the 4 school terms. Students can be enrolled at the IEC soon after arriving in Australia. The program runs for 12 months; however, it can be extended by an additional 12 months for students holding humanitarian visa subclasses.

An appointment to determine eligibility with the IEC Deputy Principal must be made prior to a student commencing. Enrolments can take up to 2 hours, and when necessary, interpreters are provided.

An interview at Ellenbrook IEC does not mean a student is or will be enrolled. The IEC Deputy Principal and the school Principal will discuss the child and their suitability for IEC enrolment before a decision is made. This discussion will take place once the student and their family have left the appointment; after this, the decision will be communicated to the parent by phone call or email.

Important: Under almost all circumstances, newly arrived students may be enrolled directly in the IEC rather than going through an enrolment process at another school first. Parents or schools may contact Mr Matt Bennett, IEC Deputy Principal or Mrs Tracie Douglas, IEC School Officer on 08 9297 7300 to make an appointment.

items.title: Ethnic Education Assistants
items.body: The IEC employs three Ethnic Education Assistants (EEAs) who are multilingual and speak second (and often third, fourth and fifth) languages as well as English. The EEAs assist teachers in the teaching and learning program and, when required, assist students and parents with interpreting. If EEAs are unable to speak a required language or are unavailable, the IEC utilises external interpreting services.

items.title: Assessment and reporting
items.body:
Ellenbrook Intensive English Centre teachers use the English as an Additional Language/Dialect (EAL/D) Progress Map to monitor, assess and report on students. The EAL/D Progress Map is a Western Australian planning, monitoring and assessment tool for students requiring support in developing Standard Australian English (SAE) who come from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, whether arriving from overseas or born in Australia. The EAL/D Progress Map is aligned to the Western Australian Curriculum and applies to all learning areas.

Students at Ellenbrook IEC are reported on each semester (at the end of Term 2 and Term 4) as per the requirements of the Department of Education's Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Policy (CAR) K to 10: Policy and Guidelines. Parent interviews are held with the student's classroom teacher to discuss the student's final report when they are due to transition from the IEC into mainstream schooling. Parents may request an interview with their child's classroom teacher at any time, but an appointment must be made. When necessary, an interpreter is provided.

items.title: Ellenbrook IEC bus transport
items.body:
The Education Department of Western Australia provides a designated bus service for students attending Intensive English Centre (IEC) programs. Access to the bus service depends on the student's visa category, distance from the IEC, and seat availability. Ellenbrook IEC buses transport students living within the Ellenbrook IEC catchment area.

All IEC buses have Bus Aides who supervise students. Students are picked up at their home in the morning and brought to Ellenbrook Primary School, then taken home in the afternoon. Parents who prefer to drive their child can park on the street outside the school or at the shopping centre that backs onto the school.

data.body: If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to call Mr Matt Bennett, IEC Deputy Principal, or Mrs Tracie Douglas, IEC School Officer, on 08 9297 7300.

title: School Hours
seo_description: Ellenbrook Primary School hours are 8.45am to 2.50pm, Monday to Friday, with classrooms open from 8.30am. See recess and lunch times for Years 1 to 6.

data.lead: Classroom doors open at 8.30am, to enable students to get ready for the day.
data.body:
The educational programs begin at 8.45am. All students should be in their classrooms and ready to start lessons by this time. If children are late to school they miss roll call, morning routines and other activities that set the context for the day.

School will start and finish at the same time for Pre-primary to Year 6 children. Kindergarten parents should consult the Kindergarten/Pre-primary Handbook.

Children should not remain at school after 2.50pm as adequate teacher supervision cannot be provided. If parents or guardians are late, children are directed to the office where they will be supervised and parents contacted. Please advise your child's teacher if the usual collection details for your child have been changed.

title: Bikes, Scooters and Skateboards
heading: Bicycles, Skateboards and Scooters
seo_description: Riding bikes and scooters to school? Read Ellenbrook Primary School's rules on helmets, walking through the grounds and locking up at the bike racks.

data.lead: It is requested that parents do all they can to ensure that children are conversant with the rules of the road (as applied to cyclists) before they permit their children to ride their bicycles on the open road.
data.body:
Children do not have the ability to judge car speeds and distances before the age of 10 years.

Rules for riding to school

  • Always wear a helmet when riding bikes, skateboards and scooters to and from school.
  • Walk bikes, skateboards and scooters to and from the bicycle racks.
  • Lock bikes with a chain. They are stored at the owner's risk.
  • Skateboards and scooters must also be left at the bike racks during the day. This is a safety matter. These too need to be locked and are the owner's responsibility.

title: Medical Information
seo_description: Children at Ellenbrook Primary with an allergy or medical condition need a Medical Plan lodged with the office. Read how medication is managed at school.

data.lead: Any child who has an allergy or medical condition will need to have a detailed Medical Plan submitted to the office. Parents must update this plan if medical advice changes.
data.body:
School staff cannot administer analgesics. If a child is required to have prescribed medicine at school, parents must advise the administration and teacher of all relevant details.

Medication at school

  • Parents provide written authority on the form available from the school office, or by completing Form 3 Administration of Medication and handing it into the office.
  • Parents need to obtain a letter from the doctor noting the need for medication during school hours.
  • Parents must hand medication to office staff and collect medication. It will not be handed to any underage person.
  • Parents provide in writing all details relevant to the use of the medication.
  • Medication must be in an original dispensing package or bottle clearly marked with the doctor's instructions.
  • Medication will be kept in the school office.
  • All staff that have the child in their care will be advised.

Teachers and office staff cannot be expected to administer prescribed medication or treatments which require specialist training. It is the parents' responsibility to provide adequate information regarding the child's condition and action or treatment under emergency conditions.
